option_description: Controls whether a secrets scanner has identified credentials, API keys, certificates, or tokens embedded in any layer of the container image, including historically overwritten or deleted layers that remain accessible in the OCI layer manifest.
security_impact: Directly triggers the embedded_secrets_in_image_layers Rego rule when true and enforcement is scan_only or none. Because OCI layer blobs are immutable and permanently readable from the manifest, secrets added and later 'deleted' in a subsequent Dockerfile layer remain fully recoverable. This is a high-criticality exposure (score 8) mapped to MITRE T1552.001 and T1525.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Export the full image as a tar archive and run Trivy secrets scan across all layers, including non-final blobs.
how_to_obtain.command: docker save <image>:<tag> -o image.tar && trivy image --input image.tar --scanners secret --format json | jq '.Results[] | select(.Secrets != null) | {Target, Secrets}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON output listing any secret findings with the layer target path. An empty Results array or null Secrets fields indicates no secrets detected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use truffleHog to scan the extracted image tar with full layer coverage, outputting structured JSON results.
how_to_obtain.command: docker save <image>:<tag> | trufflehog docker --image=file://- --json 2>/dev/null | jq '{found: (. != null)}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: truffleHog outputs a JSON object per finding. No output or empty stream indicates no secrets found across any layer.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Manually extract individual layer blobs from the image tar and run detect-secrets on each blob to confirm per-layer findings.
how_to_obtain.command: mkdir -p /tmp/img_layers && tar -xf image.tar -C /tmp/img_layers && for layer in /tmp/img_layers/*/layer.tar; do echo "=== $layer ==="; tar -xOf "$layer" 2>/dev/null | detect-secrets scan --list-all-plugins; done
how_to_obtain.expected_output: detect-secrets outputs a secrets.json per layer. Any non-empty 'results' key with findings sets this attribute to true.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Harbor registry, navigate to the repository, select the image tag, and open the 'Vulnerabilities' or 'Security' scan tab to review secrets scan results if Harbor is configured with a Trivy adapter.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor UI → Projects → <project> → Repositories → <repo> → Tags → <tag> → Security tab → Secrets section
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A populated secrets finding list with layer references indicates true. An empty or 'No issues found' state indicates false.

option_description: Controls whether at least one secret exists in a layer that is not the topmost (final) layer of the image — capturing the specific OCI layered model risk where developers attempt to delete secrets in a later RUN layer but the earlier layer blob permanently retains them in the manifest.
security_impact: Unconditionally triggers the embedded_secrets_in_image_layers Rego rule regardless of enforcement mode — meaning even enforced scanning does not suppress this exposure. This reflects that once a secret is baked into a non-final layer, no pipeline gate can remediate it without rebuilding the image from scratch. This directly maps to MITRE T1552.001 and represents a permanent, irremediable disclosure in the current image artifact.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Extract each layer blob independently from the image tar and scan only non-final layers for secrets using Trivy, comparing layer indices against the manifest order.
how_to_obtain.command:
docker save <image>:<tag> -o image.tar && python3 -c "
import json, subprocess, tarfile, os, tempfile
with tarfile.open('image.tar') as t:
    manifest = json.load(t.extractfile('manifest.json'))
    layers = manifest[0]['Layers']
    for i, layer in enumerate(layers[:-1]):
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix='.tar', delete=False) as tmp:
            tmp.write(t.extractfile(layer).read())
            tmp_path = tmp.name
        result = subprocess.run(['trivy','fs','--scanners','secret','--format','json',tmp_path], capture_output=True, text=True)
        findings = json.loads(result.stdout)
        if any(r.get('Secrets') for r in findings.get('Results',[])):
            print(f'Layer {i} (non-final): SECRET FOUND in {layer}')
        os.unlink(tmp_path)
"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Script prints layer index and path for any non-final layer containing secrets. No output indicates no secrets in non-final layers.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use crane to extract the image manifest layer list and run truffleHog on each layer blob digest individually via the registry API, checking all but the last entry.
how_to_obtain.command: crane manifest <registry>/<image>:<tag> | jq -r '.layers[:-1][].digest' | while read digest; do echo "Scanning non-final layer: $digest"; crane blob <registry>/<image>@$digest | trufflehog filesystem /dev/stdin --json 2>/dev/null; done
how_to_obtain.expected_output: truffleHog JSON output for each non-final layer blob. Any finding object present sets this attribute to true.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run docker history to identify which Dockerfile layers added sensitive files, then correlate with trivy findings layer targets to identify non-final layer secrets.
how_to_obtain.command: docker history --no-trunc <image>:<tag> --format '{{.ID}} {{.CreatedBy}}' && trivy image --scanners secret --format json <image>:<tag> | jq '[.Results[] | select(.Secrets != null) | {target: .Target, secrets: [.Secrets[].Title]}]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Trivy JSON lists targets by layer path. Cross-reference with history output — any secret in a layer that is not the final entry in the history sets this attribute to true.

option_description: Controls the enforcement posture of secrets scanning within the registry or CI/CD pipeline — whether secret findings block image push/promotion (enforced), are reported only (scan_only), or no scanning is configured at all (none).
security_impact: Determines whether the embedded_secrets_in_image_layers Rego rule fires in combination with secrets_detected_in_layers. When set to scan_only or none, a detected secret in any layer will trigger the high-criticality exposure. The enforced state provides the only pipeline-level control preventing new secret-laden images from reaching the registry, though it cannot remediate secrets already present in non-final layers (which trigger the rule unconditionally).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the CI/CD pipeline configuration file for secrets scanning step definitions and failure conditions that block pipeline progression.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E '(trivy|trufflehog|detect-secrets|gitleaks|secret)' .gitlab-ci.yml .github/workflows/*.yml Jenkinsfile 2>/dev/null | grep -E '(allow_failure|exit|fail|block|gate)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Pipeline steps with secrets scanning and no 'allow_failure: true' or equivalent indicate enforced. Scanning steps with allow_failure or no blocking exit codes indicate scan_only. Absence of scanning steps indicates none.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the Harbor registry API for webhook and robot account configurations, and check if admission policies block pushes on secret findings.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u admin:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project>/webhook/policies' | jq '.[] | {name, event_types, enabled}' && curl -s -u admin:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project>/scanner' | jq '{name, capabilities}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active webhook policies that trigger on push events combined with a configured scanner with secret capabilities suggest enforced. Scanner present without blocking webhook indicates scan_only.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In AWS ECR, check the registry scanning configuration under Scan on push settings, and verify if scan failures are connected to any CodePipeline approval gate.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console → ECR → Repositories → <repository> → Edit scanning settings → Review 'Scan on push' toggle; then CodePipeline → <pipeline> → Review stages for ECR scan approval actions
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Scan on push enabled with a pipeline approval gate blocking on HIGH/CRITICAL findings = enforced. Scan on push enabled without gate = scan_only. Scan on push disabled = none.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the CI/CD runbook or developer documentation to determine if secrets scanning is documented as a required gate versus an advisory step.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documentation explicitly stating pipeline fails and blocks promotion on secret findings = enforced. Documentation describing scan results as informational or requiring manual review = scan_only. No documentation of secrets scanning = none.

option_description: Controls the declared data classification tier assigned to this container image, representing both the operational environment tier (production_high, development, public) and the data sensitivity level (confidential, restricted, internal). This label drives classification enforcement and encryption policy decisions across multiple Rego rules.
security_impact: Used as the primary condition gate in two Rego rules: missing_classification_label_enforcement fires when tier is production_high without a manifest label or verification enforcement; unencrypted_image_layer_storage_at_rest fires for confidential/restricted images without image-level encryption. Defaulting to unclassified means images without explicit labels may bypass encryption requirements while still triggering the internal/unclassified encryption exposure rule.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the image manifest labels and OCI annotations using docker inspect and crane to extract the classification label value.
how_to_obtain.command: docker inspect <image>:<tag> | jq '.[0].Config.Labels' && crane config <registry>/<image>:<tag> | jq '.config.Labels' && crane manifest <registry>/<image>:<tag> | jq '.annotations'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output shows label keys such as 'com.example.classification', 'org.opencontainers.image.classification', or similar. The value maps to one of the enum tiers. Missing or null label = unclassified.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the CI/CD pipeline build arguments and Dockerfile for classification label definitions applied at build time.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E '(LABEL|classification|data.class|sensitivity|tier)' Dockerfile* && grep -E '(classification|CLASSIFICATION)' .gitlab-ci.yml .github/workflows/*.yml Jenkinsfile 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: LABEL instructions with classification keys and tier values confirm the build-time classification assignment. Absence indicates the image relies on runtime labeling or is unclassified.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Retrieve the image manifest directly from the registry API and parse the config blob for label metadata.
how_to_obtain.command: TOKEN=$(curl -s 'https://<registry>/token?service=<registry>&scope=repository:<image>:pull' | jq -r .token) && MANIFEST=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Accept: application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json' 'https://<registry>/v2/<image>/manifests/<tag>') && CONFIG_DIGEST=$(echo $MANIFEST | jq -r .config.digest) && curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 'https://<registry>/v2/<image>/blobs/'$CONFIG_DIGEST | jq '.config.Labels'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON object of all image labels. Classification key presence with a valid enum value confirms the tier. Null or missing key = unclassified.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Harbor, navigate to the image tag details page and review the Labels section for classification metadata applied via Harbor label management or OCI annotations.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor UI → Projects → <project> → Repositories → <repo> → Tags → <tag> → Click tag name → Scroll to Labels / Annotations section
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Labels panel shows classification key-value pairs. No classification label present = treat as unclassified.

option_description: Controls whether the image manifest or tag metadata contains a recognized classification label with a non-empty value, as an OCI annotation or Docker label. This is the baseline metadata requirement for all classification-aware policy enforcement downstream.
security_impact: Directly triggers the missing_classification_label_enforcement Rego rule when false and image_classification_tier is production_high. Without a machine-readable classification label in the manifest, admission controllers, audit pipelines, and downstream consumers cannot programmatically apply handling controls appropriate to the image's sensitivity. This leaves production_high images indistinguishable from development or public images in automated systems.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use crane to retrieve the image config blob and check for classification-related label keys matching your organization's label schema.
how_to_obtain.command: crane config <registry>/<image>:<tag> | jq '.config.Labels | to_entries | map(select(.key | test("classif|sensitivity|data.class|tier"; "i")))'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An array with at least one entry containing a non-empty value indicates true. An empty array or null indicates the classification label is absent (false).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use docker inspect locally to check both Config.Labels and the manifest annotations for the classification label across common organizational schemas.
how_to_obtain.command: docker inspect <image>:<tag> --format='{{json .Config.Labels}}' | python3 -c "import sys,json; labels=json.load(sys.stdin); found=[k for k in labels if any(x in k.lower() for x in ['classif','sensit','tier','restrict'])]; print('FOUND:',found) if found else print('NO CLASSIFICATION LABEL')"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Script prints 'FOUND: [<label_key>]' if a classification label is present (true). Prints 'NO CLASSIFICATION LABEL' if absent (false).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check OCI image index annotations via the registry manifest API for classification annotations following OCI image spec annotation conventions.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json' 'https://<registry>/v2/<image>/manifests/<tag>' | jq '{oci_annotations: .annotations, config_digest: .config.digest}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: OCI annotations object containing classification key-value pairs = true. Null annotations or no classification key = false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Google Artifact Registry, open the image version details and check the Metadata tab for custom labels applied to the image version.
how_to_obtain.navigation: GCP Console → Artifact Registry → Repositories → <repo> → <image> → <version> → Metadata tab → Labels section
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Labels section displays classification key-value pair = true. Empty labels section or no classification key = false.

option_description: Controls whether the registry or admission control layer actively validates the presence and validity of a classification label at image push and pull time, blocking images that lack required classification metadata from being accepted or distributed.
security_impact: Second trigger condition in the missing_classification_label_enforcement Rego rule for production_high images — fires independently of whether the label is present. Even if a label exists, without enforcement at the registry boundary, developers can push mislabeled or unlabeled images into production tiers. This maps to MITRE T1204.003 and T1525, where absence of admission gates allows malicious or unvetted images to reach production environments.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect OPA/Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint objects in Kubernetes for image admission policies that verify classification labels on pod image references.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get constrainttemplates -A -o json | jq '.items[].spec.crd.spec.names.kind' && kubectl get constraints -A -o yaml | grep -A 10 -i 'classif'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ConstraintTemplate definitions with classification validation logic and active Constraint objects with enforcement action 'deny' = true. No classification-related constraints = false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the Harbor registry API for webhook policies configured to validate classification labels on push events, and check project metadata for label enforcement rules.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u admin:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project-id>/webhook/policies' | jq '.[] | select(.event_types[] | contains("PUSH_ARTIFACT")) | {name, enabled, event_types}' && curl -s -u admin:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project-id>' | jq '.metadata'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active webhook policies triggering on PUSH_ARTIFACT events connected to a classification validation endpoint = true. No push webhooks or disabled policies = false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Harbor, review the Project Policy settings for label enforcement and check if distribution rules require classification labels before pull is permitted.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor UI → Projects → <project> → Configuration → Policy tab → Review 'Prevent vulnerable images from running' and label-related policy rules; also check Administration → Labels for required label assignments
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active policies requiring specific labels before push/pull operations = true. No label-based policies configured = false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review CI/CD pipeline gate scripts and registry admission webhook source code to confirm classification label validation is implemented as a blocking check, not advisory.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -rE '(classification|label.verify|label.enforce|admission|webhook)' ./infra/opa/ ./k8s/gatekeeper/ ./registry-config/ 2>/dev/null | grep -v '.pyc'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy files with classification label validation rules and deny actions = true. No policy files or advisory-only rules = false.

option_description: Controls whether image layer blobs are encrypted at the OCI image or manifest level using dedicated cryptographic envelope encryption (such as OCI image encryption per the OCI spec), independent of underlying storage-layer or disk encryption provided by the registry host infrastructure.
security_impact: Primary condition in the unencrypted_image_layer_storage_at_rest Rego rule. For confidential/restricted images, absence of image-level encryption fires the high-criticality exposure regardless of storage encryption. For internal/unclassified images, absence combined with missing KMS also triggers the rule. Storage-layer disk encryption does not satisfy this because it does not restrict access at the image artifact level — any principal with repository storage access can read raw layer blobs without image-level encryption.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the OCI image manifest for encryption annotations indicating per-layer or envelope encryption metadata per the OCI image encryption specification.
how_to_obtain.command: crane manifest <registry>/<image>:<tag> | jq '{mediaType: .mediaType, layers: [.layers[] | {mediaType: .mediaType, digest: .digest, annotations: .annotations}]}' | grep -E '(encrypted|enc\.key|ocicrypt|isecl)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Layer mediaType values ending in '+encrypted' (e.g., 'application/vnd.oci.image.layer.v1.tar+gzip+encrypted') or ocicrypt annotations present = true. Standard mediaTypes without encryption suffix = false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use skopeo to inspect the image manifest and configuration for OCI encryption indicators including the presence of encrypted layer blobs.
how_to_obtain.command: skopeo inspect --raw docker://<registry>/<image>:<tag> | jq '.layers[] | select(.mediaType | test("encrypt"))' && skopeo inspect docker://<registry>/<image>:<tag> | jq '.LayersData[] | select(.MIMEType | test("encrypt"))'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Layers with encrypted MIME types returned from either command = true. Empty results from both commands = false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Pull the raw image manifest from the registry API and examine layer mediaType fields for OCI encryption suffixes.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Accept: application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json,application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json' 'https://<registry>/v2/<image>/manifests/<tag>' | python3 -c "import sys,json; m=json.load(sys.stdin); enc=[l for l in m.get('layers',[]) if 'encrypt' in l.get('mediaType','')]; print('ENCRYPTED LAYERS:',len(enc),'/',len(m.get('layers',[]))) "
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output showing 'ENCRYPTED LAYERS: N / N' where N > 0 = true. 'ENCRYPTED LAYERS: 0 / N' = false (image-level encryption not enabled).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the registry configuration and CI/CD pipeline build scripts for ocicrypt configuration files or imgcrypt tool usage indicating image-level encryption is applied at build or push time.
how_to_obtain.command: find . /etc/containers/ ~/.config/containers/ -name 'policy.json' -o -name 'ocicrypt.conf' -o -name '*.enc.yaml' 2>/dev/null | xargs grep -l 'encrypt\|ocicrypt\|imgcrypt' 2>/dev/null && grep -rE '(imgcrypt|ocicrypt|--encryption-key|image.encrypt)' Jenkinsfile .gitlab-ci.yml .github/workflows/*.yml 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ocicrypt.conf files with key provider configurations, or pipeline steps using imgcrypt/--encryption-key flags = true. No encryption configuration files or pipeline steps = false.

option_description: Controls whether the encryption keys used for image-level encryption are managed by an externally access-controlled Key Management Service (KMS) with policies scoped to image classification tier or team, rather than static keys stored alongside registry configuration or shared keys with broad access.
security_impact: Second condition in the unencrypted_image_layer_storage_at_rest Rego rule for confidential/restricted images — even when image_level_encryption_enabled is true, the rule still fires if this is false. Static or shared keys negate the access control benefits of image encryption because anyone who can access the registry configuration can also decrypt any image. KMS-backed keys with classification-tier policies ensure that access to production_high or confidential images requires explicit key policy authorization, not just registry credentials.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Examine the ocicrypt key provider configuration and container registry configuration for references to an external KMS endpoint rather than local keyfiles.
how_to_obtain.command: cat /etc/containers/ocicrypt/keys.conf /etc/containers/ocicrypt.conf ~/.config/containers/ocicrypt.conf 2>/dev/null | grep -E '(kms|vault|aws-kms|gcp-kms|azure-kv|endpoint|provider)' && find /etc/ ~/.config/ -name '*.pem' -o -name '*.key' 2>/dev/null | grep -i 'registry\|image\|ocicrypt' | head -20
how_to_obtain.expected_output: KMS endpoint URLs (e.g., arn:aws:kms:, projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/, https://vault.example.com) in config = true. Local .pem or .key file paths in config = false (static key, not KMS-backed).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, or HashiCorp Vault key aliases/policies that are scoped specifically to container registry encryption and tied to classification tiers.
how_to_obtain.command: aws kms list-aliases --query 'Aliases[?contains(AliasName, `container`) || contains(AliasName, `registry`) || contains(AliasName, `image`)]' --output json 2>/dev/null && vault list secret/registry/keys 2>/dev/null && gcloud kms keys list --location=global --keyring=container-registry --format=json 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: KMS aliases or Vault paths referencing registry/container/classification context = true. No classification-scoped key entries found in any KMS = false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Retrieve the KMS key policy for registry encryption keys and verify that access is restricted by classification tier tags rather than broad wildcard principals.
how_to_obtain.command: KEY_ID=$(aws kms list-aliases | jq -r '.Aliases[] | select(.AliasName | test("container|registry|image")) | .TargetKeyId' | head -1) && aws kms get-key-policy --key-id $KEY_ID --policy-name default | jq '.Policy | fromjson | .Statement[] | {Effect, Principal, Condition}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy statements with Condition blocks restricting access by resource tag (e.g., classification tier tag) or specific role ARNs per tier = true. Policy with Principal: '*' or broad role access without classification-based conditions = false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the platform or security engineering team to confirm whether static key files are stored in the registry host configuration, SCM, or secrets manager, and whether key access is audited and rotation is automated through a KMS.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -rE '(REGISTRY_KEY|ENCRYPT_KEY|IMAGE_KEY|OCIcrypt_KEY)' .env* docker-compose.yml kubernetes/secrets/*.yaml helm/*/values*.yaml 2>/dev/null | grep -v '.pyc'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No static key values in environment files or Helm values (only KMS ARN/path references) = true. Literal key material or base64-encoded static keys found in configuration files = false.

option_description: Controls whether a formal retention schedule or policy exists governing when old image tags or versions must be deleted or archived from the container registry. This is a foundational lifecycle management control that determines if any rules exist to prevent indefinite accumulation of stale images.
security_impact: The Rego policy flags 'absent_image_retention_and_expiry_policy' when retention_policy_defined is false, triggering the exposure immediately. Without a retention policy, registries accumulate stale images containing deprecated credentials, outdated dependencies with known CVEs, and superseded classified data — violating data minimization requirements. The OCI layered model compounds this risk: sensitive data from old build layers remains recoverable even if deleted in subsequent layers.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check AWS ECR for lifecycle policies on all repositories to confirm whether retention rules are configured.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr describe-lifecycle-policies --region <region> --query 'lifecyclePolicyPreviewResults[*].{repo:repositoryName,policy:lifecyclePolicyText}' 2>/dev/null || aws ecr list-repositories --query 'repositories[*].repositoryName' --output text | xargs -I{} aws ecr get-lifecycle-policy --repository-name {} --region <region> 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON output containing lifecyclePolicyText with rules; empty or AccessDeniedException indicates no policy is defined.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Google Cloud Artifact Registry or GCR for cleanup policies configured on repositories.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud artifacts repositories list --format='table(name,cleanupPolicies)' --project=<project-id> 2>/dev/null || gcloud container images list --repository=gcr.io/<project-id> --format=json | jq '.[].name'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Repositories with cleanupPolicies populated indicate a retention policy is defined; empty cleanupPolicies field indicates no policy.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Harbor registry, navigate to the project, select 'Tag Retention' under 'Policy', and verify that at least one retention rule is listed with a defined schedule.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor UI → Projects → <project-name> → Policy → Tag Retention → verify rules exist
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One or more retention rules displayed with criteria (e.g., 'retain the most recently pushed # artifacts') and an attached schedule.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect IaC definitions (Terraform or CloudFormation) for lifecycle policy resources to confirm whether retention is codified.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -r 'lifecycle_policy\|LifecyclePolicy\|cleanup_policy\|tag_retention' <iac-repo-path> --include='*.tf' --include='*.yaml' --include='*.json' -l
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Files containing lifecycle policy resource definitions confirm a policy is defined; no results indicate absent IaC-managed retention.

option_description: Controls whether automated tooling or registry-native lifecycle rules are actively configured and executing to delete or archive images per the retention policy — without requiring manual intervention. A written policy without enforcement automation does not satisfy this control.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'absent_image_retention_and_expiry_policy' when retention_policy_defined is true but image_expiry_automation_enabled is false AND stale_image_count is greater than zero. A documented policy without automation is effectively unenforced — stale images with embedded secrets or classified layer data persist indefinitely, demonstrating that policy alone is insufficient without technical enforcement backing it.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify ECR lifecycle policy rules are present and valid (presence of the policy JSON confirms automation is configured and executed by ECR natively).
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr get-lifecycle-policy --repository-name <repository-name> --region <region> --query 'lifecyclePolicyText' --output text | python3 -c "import sys,json; p=json.load(sys.stdin); print('Rules count:', len(p.get('rules',[])))" 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'Rules count: N' where N >= 1 confirms automation is enabled; error or zero rules indicates automation is absent.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Harbor tag retention execution history via API to confirm scheduled automation has actually run.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u <admin>:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project-name>/immutabletagrules' && curl -s -u <admin>:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project-name>/tagRetention' | jq '.trigger,last_executors'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON with trigger schedule (e.g., cron expression) and last execution timestamps confirms automation is active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query GCP Artifact Registry cleanup policies to confirm automated cleanup rules are enabled on all repositories.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" 'https://artifactregistry.googleapis.com/v1/projects/<project>/locations/<region>/repositories/<repo>' | jq '.cleanupPolicies'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Non-null cleanupPolicies object with at least one policy entry confirms automation is configured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the platform or DevOps team to determine if CI/CD pipelines include a garbage collection or image pruning step, and request evidence of the last execution (e.g., pipeline logs, cron job history).
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get cronjob -A | grep -i 'registry\|prune\|cleanup\|gc' 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CronJob resources or confirmed pipeline stage with recent last-run timestamp validates automated expiry enforcement.

typical_values: false (policy exists on paper but no enforcement mechanism)
true (ECR lifecycle rules, Harbor scheduled retention, GCP cleanup policies actively running)

option_description: Measures the number of image tags or versions in the registry that have not been pulled or updated beyond the organization's defined or industry-standard retention window (typically 90 days). This is a quantitative indicator of how effectively retention policies are being enforced.
security_impact: The Rego policy uses stale_image_count greater than zero as a compounding trigger for 'absent_image_retention_and_expiry_policy' when automation is disabled — even if a retention policy exists. A high stale image count indicates accumulation of images that may contain deprecated credentials, unpatched vulnerabilities, and sensitive classified layer data that should have been disposed of, directly violating data minimization principles.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query AWS ECR for images older than 90 days with no recent pull activity across all repositories.
how_to_obtain.command: CUTOFF=$(date -d '90 days ago' '+%s' 2>/dev/null || date -v-90d '+%s'); aws ecr describe-repositories --query 'repositories[*].repositoryName' --output text | tr '\t' '\n' | while read repo; do aws ecr describe-images --repository-name "$repo" --query "imageDetails[?to_number(to_string(imagePushedAt)) < \`$CUTOFF\`].{repo:'$repo',tag:imageTags[0],pushed:imagePushedAt}" --output json 2>/dev/null; done | jq -s '[.[]|.[]]|length'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An integer count of image tags pushed more than 90 days ago; 0 indicates no stale images.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use the gcloud CLI to list GCR or Artifact Registry image tags and filter those not updated within the retention threshold.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud container images list-tags gcr.io/<project>/<image> --format=json | jq --arg cutoff "$(date -d '90 days ago' --iso-8601 2>/dev/null || date -v-90d -Iseconds)" '[.[] | select(.timestamp.datetime < $cutoff)] | length'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Integer count of tags older than the cutoff date; any value above 0 indicates stale images are present.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the Harbor API for tag statistics filtered by push date to count images exceeding the retention threshold.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u <admin>:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project>/repositories/<repo>/artifacts?page_size=100&with_tag=true' | jq --arg cutoff "$(date -d '90 days ago' -Iseconds 2>/dev/null)" '[.[] | select(.push_time < $cutoff)] | length'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Count of artifacts pushed before the cutoff; registry-wide totals require iteration across all repositories.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use the AWS Console ECR image view filtered by push date to visually inspect and count stale images per repository.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console → ECR → Repositories → <repository> → Images tab → sort by 'Pushed at' column → count images older than retention threshold
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Images displayed with push timestamps; those older than the defined threshold (e.g., 90 days) constitute the stale image count.

option_description: Defines the level at which access controls are enforced within the container registry — whether grants are applied at the entire registry level, per repository, per individual image tag, or per classification tier. This determines how precisely permissions can be scoped to prevent cross-tier access.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers 'inadequate_access_control_granularity_for_classified_images' when this value is 'registry' or 'repository' AND either mixed_classification_images_in_shared_repository is true or lower_env_principals_with_production_image_access is true. Coarse-grained access at the registry or repository level means that any principal with access to a development image in a shared repository inherits read access to production image layers containing sensitive runtime configuration, secrets, and proprietary binaries.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect AWS ECR repository policies to determine whether permissions are scoped to repository-level or include tag-condition keys.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr get-repository-policy --repository-name <repository-name> --region <region> --query 'policyText' --output text | python3 -c "import sys,json; p=json.load(sys.stdin); [print(s) for s in p.get('Statement',[])]" 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer|Condition|aws:ResourceTag'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Presence of Condition blocks with ecr:ResourceTag or image-tag conditions indicates tag or classification_tier granularity; absence indicates registry or repository level.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review Harbor project role assignments to determine if permissions differentiate by tag or classification label.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u <admin>:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project-name>/members' | jq '.[] | {role_id,entity_name,entity_type}' && curl -s -u <admin>:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project-name>/immutabletagrules' | jq '.'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Role assignments at project (repository) level with no tag-level distinctions indicates 'repository' granularity; tag-conditional rules indicate finer control.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check GCP Artifact Registry IAM policy for conditional bindings that restrict access by tag or label attributes.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" -X POST 'https://artifactregistry.googleapis.com/v1/projects/<project>/locations/<region>/repositories/<repo>:getIamPolicy' | jq '.bindings[] | {role, condition, members}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Bindings with non-null condition expressions using resource.name or tag attributes indicate tag or classification_tier granularity; unconditional bindings indicate repository level.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the Azure Container Registry access control blade to determine whether access policies are scoped to repository scope tokens or applied globally.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Azure Portal → Container Registries → <registry-name> → Repository permissions → Tokens → inspect scope maps per token
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Tokens with repository-specific scope maps indicate repository-level; tokens with action-level filters per tag indicate tag granularity; single registry-wide role assignments indicate registry level.

typical_values: repository (most common default across ECR, GCR, Harbor)
registry (overly permissive, common in small teams)
tag (rare, typically only in highly regulated environments)
classification_tier (uncommon, requires custom tooling or policy enforcement)

option_description: Indicates whether a single repository or access grant scope contains images of differing classification tiers — for example, production and development images sharing the same repository or IAM binding, creating an implicit access escalation path.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers 'inadequate_access_control_granularity_for_classified_images' under two conditions involving this attribute: when access_control_granularity_level is 'registry' or 'repository' AND this is true, or when both this attribute and lower_env_principals_with_production_image_access are true regardless of granularity level. Mixing classification tiers in shared repositories means that any principal with access to lower-tier images effectively gains access to production-classified layers, negating classification-based access separation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate ECR repository image tags and inspect OCI annotation labels for classification markers to identify repositories containing images with multiple classification labels.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr list-repositories --output text --query 'repositories[*].repositoryName' | tr '\t' '\n' | while read repo; do echo "=== $repo ==="; aws ecr describe-images --repository-name "$repo" --query 'imageDetails[*].imageTags' --output json | jq -r '.[][] | select(test("prod|dev|staging|confidential|internal|restricted"; "i"))'; done
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Repositories that display a mix of prod/dev/staging or classification-level tags indicate mixed classification images in a shared repository.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use docker inspect or skopeo to read OCI image manifest annotations for classification labels across images in the same repository.
how_to_obtain.command: skopeo inspect docker://<registry-host>/<repo>:<tag> 2>/dev/null | jq '.Labels | {"io.classification", "classification", "data-classification"}' | grep -v null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Different classification label values across multiple tags within the same repository confirms mixed classification; consistent or absent labels require policy review.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query Harbor artifact API to retrieve all artifacts in a repository with their labels and determine if multiple classification-tier labels coexist.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u <admin>:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project>/repositories/<repo>/artifacts?with_label=true&page_size=100' | jq '[.[] | {tags: [.tags[].name], labels: [.labels[].name]}]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Artifacts with labels spanning multiple classification tiers (e.g., 'production' and 'development') in the same repository confirm the mixed state.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview development and platform teams to understand their repository naming and organization conventions, and whether classification separation by repository is enforced as a policy.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Confirmed policy of one-classification-tier-per-repository with enforced repository naming conventions resolves this concern; absence of such policy confirms the risk.

typical_values: true (common in small teams using monorepo-style registry organization)
false (enterprises with enforced repository-per-tier policies or separate registries per environment)

option_description: Indicates whether service accounts or users authorized only for development or staging images have effective read access to production image layers due to coarse-grained access grants. This captures the real-world permission outcome rather than just the policy intent.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires 'inadequate_access_control_granularity_for_classified_images' when access_control_granularity_level is 'registry' or 'repository' AND this is true, or when both this and mixed_classification_images_in_shared_repository are true. Development CI/CD service accounts inheriting production image pull permissions can extract production secrets, proprietary binaries, and classified runtime configuration embedded in image layers — a direct privilege escalation path exploiting coarse registry permissions (MITRE T1213.003).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Simulate effective ECR permissions for a known development CI/CD service account against production repositories using the AWS policy simulator.
how_to_obtain.command: aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:role/<dev-ci-role> --action-names ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer ecr:BatchGetImage --resource-arns arn:aws:ecr:<region>:<account-id>:repository/<production-repo> --query 'EvaluationResults[*].{Action:EvalActionName,Decision:EvalDecision}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'allowed' decision for ecr:BatchGetImage or ecr:GetDownloadUrlForLayer against the production repository confirms lower-env principal access.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Extract all principals with pull permissions on a production ECR repository and cross-reference against known dev/staging role naming patterns.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr get-repository-policy --repository-name <prod-repository> --region <region> --query 'policyText' --output text | python3 -c "import sys,json; p=json.load(sys.stdin); [print(s['Principal']) for s in p.get('Statement',[]) if any(a in str(s.get('Action','')) for a in ['BatchGetImage','GetDownloadUrlForLayer'])]" | grep -iE 'dev|staging|ci|build|test'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Principal ARNs containing dev/staging/CI identifiers confirm lower-environment principals have production image access.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check GCP Artifact Registry IAM bindings on production repositories for service accounts associated with development namespaces or CI runners.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud artifacts repositories get-iam-policy <prod-repo> --location=<region> --project=<project> --format=json | jq '.bindings[] | select(.members[] | test("dev|staging|ci|builder")) | {role, members}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Bindings with roles/artifactregistry.reader or broader on production repos for dev-pattern principals confirm the exposure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review registry audit logs to identify actual pull events from development service accounts against production image repositories.
how_to_obtain.command: aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=BatchGetImage --start-time $(date -d '30 days ago' -Iseconds 2>/dev/null) --query 'Events[*].{Time:EventTime,User:Username,Resources:Resources[*].ResourceName}' | grep -E '<dev-sa-pattern>|<ci-runner-pattern>' | grep '<prod-repo>'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Audit log entries showing dev/CI principals pulling from production repositories confirm effective cross-tier access is occurring.

typical_values: true (common when registry-level IAM roles grant blanket pull access to all repositories)
false (organizations with separate registries per environment or tag-conditional IAM policies)

option_description: Indicates whether the container registry has cross-region or cross-zone replication configured, causing image layer blobs and manifests to be physically transmitted across geographic boundaries and stored in multiple jurisdictions.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers 'cross_border_transfer_of_classified_image_data' when geo_replication_enabled is true AND image_classification_label is 'confidential', 'restricted', or 'secret' AND either cross_border_transfer_policy_enforced is absent or replication_audit_logging_enabled is absent. Replication of classified image layers across jurisdictions may violate data residency regulations (GDPR, PDPA, data sovereignty laws) and enables cross-border data transfer of sensitive application logic (MITRE T1537), potentially without organizational consent or regulatory authorization.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check AWS ECR registry-level replication configuration to determine if cross-region replication rules are defined.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr describe-registry --region <region> --query 'replicationConfiguration.rules' --output json 2>/dev/null | jq '.[] | {destinations: [.destinations[].region], repositoryFilters}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Non-empty rules array with destination regions confirms geo-replication is enabled; empty array or null indicates no replication.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List Azure Container Registry replications to identify all configured geographic replication locations.
how_to_obtain.command: az acr replication list --registry <registry-name> --resource-group <rg-name> --query '[*].{name:name,location:location,status:status.displayStatus}' --output table 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Table showing additional locations beyond the primary registry location confirms geo-replication is enabled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query GCP Artifact Registry repository configuration to check if multi-region or cross-region locations are configured.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" 'https://artifactregistry.googleapis.com/v1/projects/<project>/locations/<region>/repositories/<repo>' | jq '{location: .name, mode: .mode, virtualRepositoryConfig: .virtualRepositoryConfig}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A multi-region location (e.g., 'us', 'eu') or virtualRepositoryConfig pointing to multiple upstream repos confirms cross-region distribution.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect Harbor registry replication rules to identify any push-based replication endpoints in different geographic locations.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor UI → Administration → Replications → verify any replication rules exist with destination registry endpoints in different regions
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active replication rules with remote registry endpoints confirm geo-replication is enabled; no rules indicates replication is disabled.

typical_values: true (global SaaS platforms, disaster recovery configurations, CDN-optimized pull-through caches)

option_description: The data classification level assigned to a container image, derived from OCI manifest labels or registry tag conventions, reflecting the sensitivity of embedded application logic, secrets, or regulated data within its layers. This label is the primary input for cross-border transfer and disposal policy evaluation.
security_impact: The Rego policy uses image_classification_label as the primary gate for 'cross_border_transfer_of_classified_image_data' — only triggering when the value is 'confidential', 'restricted', or 'secret'. Without accurate classification labels, high-sensitivity images default to 'unclassified', causing policy rules to miss actual violations. The OCI layered model means that even deleted layer data containing classified information persists and remains subject to classification controls — making accurate labeling critical for all lifecycle and disposal policy enforcement.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect OCI image manifest annotations and Docker labels for classification markers using skopeo without pulling the full image.
how_to_obtain.command: skopeo inspect docker://<registry-host>/<repository>:<tag> | jq '{labels: .Labels, annotations: .Annotations} | with_entries(select(.value | (type == "object" and . != {})))'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Labels object containing keys such as 'io.classification', 'data-classification', 'security.classification', or 'classification' with values matching the classification scheme.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query AWS ECR image manifest for OCI annotations to extract classification labels from image configuration.
how_to_obtain.command: MANIFEST=$(aws ecr batch-get-image --repository-name <repo> --image-ids imageTag=<tag> --region <region> --query 'images[0].imageManifest' --output text); CONFIG_DIGEST=$(echo $MANIFEST | python3 -c "import sys,json; m=json.load(sys.stdin); print(m['config']['digest'])"); aws ecr get-download-url-for-layer --repository-name <repo> --layer-digest $CONFIG_DIGEST --region <region> | xargs curl -s | jq '.config.Labels'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON Labels object; absence of classification keys or null value indicates the image should be treated as 'unclassified' per the default.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Scan Harbor artifacts API for classification labels applied to images across a project.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u <admin>:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project>/repositories/<repo>/artifacts?with_label=true&page_size=50' | jq '.[] | {tags: [.tags[].name], classification_labels: [.labels[] | select(.name | test("class|sensitive|tier|confidential|restricted"; "i")) | .name]}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Artifacts with classification_labels populated confirm labeling is present; empty arrays indicate unclassified or unlabeled images.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the organization's image build pipeline (Dockerfile templates, CI/CD configurations) to confirm whether classification labels are injected at build time and validated at push time.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -r 'LABEL\|io.classification\|data-classification\|classification' <dockerfile-repo-path> --include='Dockerfile*' --include='*.dockerfile' -l
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Dockerfiles containing LABEL instructions with classification keys confirm build-time labeling; absent labels indicate classification is not enforced in the build pipeline.

typical_values: unclassified (default; most images in public or development registries lack explicit labels)
internal (common for proprietary application images without regulated data)
confidential (images containing environment-specific configs, internal API keys)
restricted (images embedding PII handlers, payment processing logic)
secret (rare; images containing cryptographic material or highly sensitive business logic)

option_description: Controls whether a verified policy or technical gate (such as OPA admission webhooks, cloud provider data residency policies, or registry replication rules) actively validates and enforces jurisdiction compliance before image layers are replicated or pulled across geographic regions.
security_impact: In the Rego policy, the cross_border_transfer_of_classified_image_data rule fires when geo_replication_enabled is true, the image carries a confidential/restricted/secret classification label, and cross_border_transfer_policy_enforced is false. Without this control, classified image manifests and layer blobs may traverse jurisdictions with conflicting data residency laws (GDPR, data localization statutes) without consent or enforcement, satisfying adversary objectives aligned with T1537 (Transfer Data to Cloud Account).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query OPA or Gatekeeper for constraint policies that reference image replication or cross-region pull operations in a Kubernetes environment.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get constraints -A -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.match.kinds[]?.apiGroups | contains([""]) or (.metadata.annotations // {} | to_entries[].value | test("replication|cross.region|residency"; "i"))) | {name: .metadata.name, kind: .kind}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One or more constraint objects referencing replication or residency enforcement; empty output indicates no active policy gate.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR, check replication configuration and Service Control Policies (SCPs) that restrict cross-region replication destinations.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr describe-registry --query 'replicationConfiguration' --output json && aws organizations list-policies --filter SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY --query 'Policies[*].{Name:Name,Id:Id}' --output table
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Replication rules scoped to approved regions; SCPs showing Deny on ecr:ReplicateImage or ecr:BatchGetImage for non-approved regions.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Azure Container Registry, navigate to the registry → Geo-replication blade and confirm only approved regions are listed. Then review Policy → Azure Policy assignments for the registry scope to identify any 'Container Registry should have geo-replication restricted to approved regions' initiative.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Azure Portal → Container Registries → [Registry Name] → Geo-replication; then [Registry Name] → Policies
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Replication targets limited to compliant regions; a policy assignment in Audit or Deny effect covering cross-region restrictions.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the registry or platform engineering team to confirm whether a documented, audited process exists that gates cross-region replication approvals. Request evidence of the last policy review or audit log showing enforcement.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A written procedure, runbook, or change-management record demonstrating active enforcement and a dated audit trail of cross-border transfer decisions.

typical_values: true (only in regulated industries with mature policy-as-code pipelines)

option_description: Controls whether the registry platform captures and retains audit log entries for every image pull and replication event, including source and destination region metadata, enabling reconstruction of which layer blobs traversed which jurisdictions.
security_impact: The Rego rule cross_border_transfer_of_classified_image_data fires independently when geo_replication_enabled is true, image_classification_label is classified, and replication_audit_logging_enabled is false — even if a transfer policy exists. Without this logging, there is no forensic trail to prove compliance with data residency obligations or to detect unauthorized cross-border pulls, directly supporting adversary data exfiltration via T1530 (Data from Cloud Storage) without leaving evidence.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR, verify CloudTrail is capturing registry data-plane events including BatchGetImage and replication actions by checking the trail configuration and querying recent events.
how_to_obtain.command: aws cloudtrail get-event-selectors --trail-name $(aws cloudtrail describe-trails --query 'trailList[0].TrailARN' --output text) --query 'EventSelectors[*].{ReadWrite:ReadWriteType,DataResources:DataResources}' && aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=BatchGetImage --max-results 5 --query 'Events[*].{Time:EventTime,Source:EventSource,Region:CloudTrailEvent}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: EventSelectors showing ReadWriteType All or ReadOnly with ECR as a data resource; recent BatchGetImage events with region and source IP metadata.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GCP Artifact Registry or GCR, verify that Data Access audit logs (DATA_READ) are enabled for the artifactregistry.googleapis.com service in the relevant project's IAM Audit Config.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud projects get-iam-policy $(gcloud config get-value project) --format=json | jq '.auditConfigs[] | select(.service == "artifactregistry.googleapis.com" or .service == "allServices") | {service: .service, logTypes: [.auditLogConfigs[].logType]}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Entry for artifactregistry.googleapis.com showing DATA_READ in logTypes; absence indicates pull events are not logged.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Azure Container Registry, navigate to Monitoring → Diagnostic settings. Confirm a diagnostic setting exists that routes ContainerRegistryRepositoryEvents and ContainerRegistryLoginEvents categories to a Log Analytics workspace or storage account.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Azure Portal → Container Registries → [Registry Name] → Monitoring → Diagnostic settings
how_to_obtain.expected_output: At least one diagnostic setting with ContainerRegistryRepositoryEvents enabled and a valid destination sink (Log Analytics, Event Hub, or Storage).

how_to_obtain.instruction: For self-hosted Harbor registries, check the Harbor admin log configuration and query recent replication job logs to confirm source/destination region metadata is captured.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u admin:$HARBOR_PASS 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/replication/executions?page=1&page_size=10' | jq '[.[] | {id:.id, policy_id:.policy_id, status:.status, start_time:.start_time, end_time:.end_time}]' && grep -E 'replication|pull|push' /var/log/harbor/core.log | tail -50
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Replication execution records with timestamps and policy references; log lines showing source/destination registry URLs for each transfer.

typical_values: false (common in self-hosted registries without explicit log sink configuration)
true (standard in cloud-native registries when diagnostic settings are explicitly enabled)

option_description: Controls whether an explicit garbage collection (GC) cycle has been executed after image deletion operations and confirmed to have purged unreferenced layer blobs from registry blob storage, not merely removed manifest and tag references.
security_impact: The Rego rule non_compliant_image_disposal_without_layer_blob_purge fires when either deleted_images_with_sensitive_classification is true or unreferenced_blob_retention_days exceeds 7, and garbage_collection_verified_post_deletion is false. Due to the OCI layered model, deleting a tag or manifest leaves underlying blobs fully intact and recoverable. Without verified GC, sensitive layer data persists indefinitely in blob storage, violating secure disposal requirements and enabling data recovery by adversaries or unauthorized insiders (T1070.004 — File Deletion bypass).

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Docker Distribution (registry:2) or Harbor, check the GC audit log or admin job history to confirm the last successful GC run timestamp.
how_to_obtain.command:
# Harbor: query GC history via API
curl -s -u admin:$HARBOR_PASS 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/system/gc?page=1&page_size=5' | jq '[.[] | {id:.id, job_status:.job_status, creation_time:.creation_time, update_time:.update_time}]'
# Docker Distribution: check container logs for GC completion
docker logs registry 2>&1 | grep -i 'garbage collect' | tail -20
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Harbor: GC job entries with job_status 'Success' and a recent creation_time. Docker Distribution: log lines confirming 'garbage collection completed' with blob deletion counts.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR, verify that lifecycle policies are configured and have executed, which triggers ECR's internal image expiration. Then check that no unreferenced layers remain by comparing image layer SHAs to stored blobs.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr get-lifecycle-policy --repository-name <repo-name> --query 'lifecyclePolicyText' --output text && aws ecr list-images --repository-name <repo-name> --filter tagStatus=UNTAGGED --query 'imageIds[*]' --output table
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A lifecycle policy JSON with rules covering untagged images; empty imageIds table indicates no unreferenced images remain after ECR's managed GC.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Harbor, navigate to Administration → Garbage Collection. Review the Job History tab to confirm the last GC run date, status, and whether it operated in delete mode (not dry-run).
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor Admin UI → Administration → Garbage Collection → Job History
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A completed (not dry-run) GC job with status 'Success' dated after the most recent image deletion event.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify blob storage inventory before and after GC to confirm unreferenced blobs were removed. For S3-backed registries, compare object counts in the blobs/ prefix pre- and post-GC.
how_to_obtain.command:
# Count blobs in S3-backed Docker Distribution storage
aws s3 ls s3://<registry-bucket>/docker/registry/v2/blobs/sha256/ --recursive --summarize | grep 'Total Objects'
# Repeat after GC and compare counts
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Reduced object count in the blobs prefix after GC run; if count is unchanged after deletion events, GC has not run or did not purge blobs.

typical_values: false (default — GC is not automatic in most self-hosted registries; Harbor and Docker Distribution require manual or scheduled triggers)
true (achieved only with confirmed scheduled or manual GC execution post-deletion)

option_description: Identifies whether any images carrying sensitive classification metadata (labels, tag prefixes, or classification annotations indicating secrets, PII, or confidential configuration) have had their manifests or tags removed but have not yet had their underlying layer blobs purged via a verified garbage collection cycle.
security_impact: This attribute directly triggers the non_compliant_image_disposal_without_layer_blob_purge Rego rule when true and garbage_collection_verified_post_deletion is false. Because OCI image deletion removes only manifest references — not blob data — sensitive layer content remains fully recoverable in blob storage. This represents a critical disposal failure for regulated data classes: decommissioned images containing hardcoded credentials, PII, or cryptographic material remain extractable by anyone with registry storage access, enabling residual data recovery aligned with T1070.009 (Clear Persistence failure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate recently deleted image tags from audit logs and cross-reference against classification labels. For Harbor, query the audit log for DELETE events on images and check their last-known labels.
how_to_obtain.command:
# Harbor: find recent DELETE audit events for images
curl -s -u admin:$HARBOR_PASS 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/audit-logs?operation=delete&resource_type=artifact&page_size=50' | jq '[.[] | {resource: .resource, operation: .operation, op_time: .op_time, username: .username}]'
# Cross-reference with label-sensitive images in remaining artifacts
curl -s -u admin:$HARBOR_PASS 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project>/repositories/<repo>/artifacts?with_label=true' | jq '[.[] | select(.labels[]?.name | test("sensitive|confidential|restricted|pii|secret"; "i")) | {digest: .digest, tags: [.tags[].name], labels: [.labels[].name]}]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: DELETE audit log entries for artifacts; if any deleted artifact names match sensitive classification patterns and GC has not run since deletion, this attribute is true.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query cloud-native audit logs for image deletion events and compare against a classification inventory. For AWS ECR with CloudTrail, identify BatchDeleteImage events and check if the deleted image tags followed a sensitive naming convention.
how_to_obtain.command: aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=BatchDeleteImage --start-time $(date -d '30 days ago' --iso-8601) --query 'Events[*].CloudTrailEvent' --output text | python3 -c "import sys,json; [print(json.dumps({k:v for k,v in json.loads(l).items() if k in ['eventTime','requestParameters','userIdentity']}, indent=2)) for l in sys.stdin if l.strip()]"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: BatchDeleteImage events with imageIds (tags/digests) that can be matched against a sensitive image classification registry or naming convention list.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GCP Artifact Registry, use the Operations API to list delete operations on tagged artifacts, then cross-reference with image labels stored in Container Analysis metadata.
how_to_obtain.command:
gcloud artifacts operations list --location=<region> --project=<project> --filter='metadata.type:DeleteVersion' --format='json' | jq '[.[] | {name:.name, done:.done, metadata:.metadata}]'
# Check Container Analysis for vulnerability/classification notes on those digests
gcloud beta container images describe <IMAGE_DIGEST> --show-package-vulnerability
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Delete operation records for artifact versions; Container Analysis notes indicating sensitivity classifications on those digests.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the image classification registry or CMDB maintained by the registry team. Identify any entries marked for decommission or recently removed that carry a sensitive data classification, and confirm whether GC was triggered as part of the disposal workflow.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A spreadsheet, CMDB record, or ticketing system entry showing sensitive-classified images marked as deleted, with a corresponding GC execution confirmation or absence thereof.

typical_values: false (ideal state — no sensitive images deleted without subsequent GC)
true (common in environments without automated GC pipelines or formal disposal workflows for classified images)

option_description: Measures the number of elapsed days between the most recent image deletion event (which should have triggered blob disposal) and the present, during which unreferenced layer blobs continue to persist in registry blob storage without a confirmed garbage collection purge. A value of 0 indicates same-day purge; higher values indicate accumulating disposal debt.
security_impact: The Rego rule non_compliant_image_disposal_without_layer_blob_purge fires when unreferenced_blob_retention_days exceeds 7 and garbage_collection_verified_post_deletion is false, regardless of image classification. Extended blob retention after deletion means sensitive layer data — including secrets embedded in non-final layers (a compounding risk of the OCI layered model) — remains recoverable for the entire retention window. This directly violates data minimization and secure disposal requirements, and the longer the window, the greater the exposure surface for T1070.004 (File Deletion bypass) and T1485.001 (Lifecycle-Triggered Deletion failure).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Determine the date of the last image deletion event and the last verified GC run, then calculate the difference. For Harbor, extract both timestamps from the API and compute the delta.
how_to_obtain.command:
# Get last deletion event timestamp
LAST_DELETE=$(curl -s -u admin:$HARBOR_PASS 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/audit-logs?operation=delete&resource_type=artifact&page_size=1' | jq -r '.[0].op_time')
# Get last successful GC run timestamp
LAST_GC=$(curl -s -u admin:$HARBOR_PASS 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/system/gc?page=1&page_size=10' | jq -r '[.[] | select(.job_status=="Success")] | .[0].update_time')
# Calculate delta in days
python3 -c "from datetime import datetime; d=datetime.fromisoformat('$LAST_DELETE'.replace('Z','+00:00')); g=datetime.fromisoformat('$LAST_GC'.replace('Z','+00:00')); print(f'Unreferenced blob retention days: {(d-g).days if d > g else 0}')"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A numeric day count; values above 7 are policy violations per the Rego rule. Negative or zero values indicate GC ran after or on the same day as deletion.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For S3-backed or object-storage-backed registries, query the blob store for objects whose last-modified date predates the most recent GC run, indicating unreferenced blobs that should have been purged.
how_to_obtain.command:
# List blobs in registry storage older than 7 days with no recent access
aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket <registry-bucket> --prefix docker/registry/v2/blobs/sha256/ --query 'Contents[?LastModified<=`'$(date -d '7 days ago' --iso-8601)'`].[Key,LastModified,Size]' --output table | head -50
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Table of blob objects older than 7 days; non-empty results indicate unreferenced blobs persisting beyond acceptable retention windows.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review cloud-provider audit logs to find the most recent image deletion event timestamp, then compare against GC execution records to establish the actual retention gap.
how_to_obtain.command:
# AWS: find most recent ECR image deletion
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=BatchDeleteImage --max-results 1 --query 'Events[0].{Time:EventTime,Detail:CloudTrailEvent}' --output json
# Compare with last ECR lifecycle policy evaluation (ECR manages GC internally via lifecycle policies)
aws ecr describe-lifecycle-policy-preview --repository-name <repo-name> --query 'previewDetails[0].{appliedRulePriority:appliedRulePriority,imageDigest:imageDigest,imagePushedAt:imagePushedAt}' 2>/dev/null || echo 'No preview active; check lifecycle policy last run via CloudWatch Events'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Timestamps for the most recent deletion and GC/lifecycle evaluation events; the day difference is the unreferenced_blob_retention_days value.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Docker Distribution v2 (self-hosted), directly inspect the registry storage filesystem or object store to identify blobs not referenced by any current manifest, using the registry's built-in garbage-collect command in dry-run mode.
how_to_obtain.command:
# Run GC in dry-run mode to identify unreferenced blobs without deleting them
docker run --rm -v /path/to/registry/config.yml:/etc/docker/registry/config.yml \
  -v /path/to/registry/data:/var/lib/registry \
  registry:2 garbage-collect --dry-run /etc/docker/registry/config.yml 2>&1 | grep -E 'blob eligible|mark|sweep|eligible for deletion'
# Count unreferenced blobs identified
docker run --rm ... registry:2 garbage-collect --dry-run /etc/docker/registry/config.yml 2>&1 | grep 'eligible for deletion' | wc -l
how_to_obtain.expected_output: List of blob digests eligible for deletion; non-zero count confirms unreferenced blobs exist. Cross-reference blob creation dates against deletion log timestamps to compute retention days.

typical_values: 1-7 (acceptable in environments with weekly GC schedules)
8-30 (common in environments with manual GC processes or infrequent maintenance windows)
30+ (problematic — indicates GC is absent, disabled, or not integrated into deletion workflows)
